author: Langorn
subject: Holy Priest Guide
content_md:
Hello everyone, Picodon here, Holy priest. I wanted to share a quick priest guide i made, mostly for new players, hope it will be useful.
---
 **DISCLAIMER** I am not a professional priest neither am i a long time player on turtle wow. Hovewer i’ve been playing private wow servers for a while.
While searching on the forum, I didn’t find a beginner oriented guide for priests that would have helped me on my journey. I hope this one will help new priests players.
I do not say that i have the absolute truth backed by complex calculations, experienced players might find my guide not accurate enough and i would be more than happy to share about it in the comments as long as people remain normal and constructive human beings.

1. **Introduction**

This guide will focus on the Healing (i.e. Holy Priest). I advise to go this way after you hit 60 and intend to raid. Before this, i recommand to level as shadow or discipline (my favourite) spec since it will make solo farming WAY easier and still allow you to heal any dungeon in the game.

The priest is a great tool in raiding environment for all the utility it brings. It is a very versatile healer who can apply Heal over Time, strong and slow direct heals, fast direct heals and some strong AoE healing (only for your group sadly) as well as an instant shield. While it’s not the best at anything the Holy priest is a great and reliable healer that fits any raid composition.

 ---
2. **Leveling**

As said, leveling as a priest is way easier as shadow or discipline. Leveling as holy is possible, however it will be slower and most likely less fun, i would not advise to go for it unless you are leveling in group.

Here is a quick example of a Discipline leveling build. It allows good mana regeneration, better healing efficiency than shadow and a cool gameplay revolving around different spells and big crits giving you instant smites.

 10 – 11 : Wand Specialization : As a leveling priest you will wand, A LOT, this talent is the strongest you can pick.
 12 – 16 : Spirit tap 5/5 : It seems boring to take this early because it doesn’t give you more damage. However this talent alone will grant you a huge amount of mana regen and will make the difference between drinking every 3 pulls and almost not have to drink at all which is a CONSIDERABLE gain of time.
 17 – 21 : Divinity 5/5 : 5% crit on every holy spell is great since discipline heavily scale on crits
 22 – 26 : Divine fury 5/5 : -0.5 casting time on basically every single spell you will use, mandatory
 27 – 29 : Piercing light 3/3 : 6% Hit so you don’t miss your spells so often
 30 – 31 : Improved power word 2/2 : fortitude : Not mandatory, but i like this talent since PWF if a great buff that you will always have.
 32 – 34 : Mental agility 3/5 : Less mana used on offensive spells, renew, shield. That’s a nice talent that opens the new tiers.
 35 : Inner Focus : Every 3 min you have a free spell with more critical chance. Use it for a greater heal if you’re in a bad situation or for holy fire when you open on a monster.
 36 – 37 : Improved inner fire 2/2 : More spell power, you’re happy
 38 – 39 : Meditation 2/3 : Give you some mana regen while fighting. This is not mandatory but still good and opens the door to the real deal.
 40 – 41 : Purifying flames 2/2 : You ALWAYS open a fight with holy fire which means this talent is basically a 12% damage increase, what else ?
 42 – 44 : Searing light 3/3 : While this talent is not very reliable in early game since you don’t have a lot of critical chance. This talent gives the disco priest one of its biggest strength, instant big smites in the head of your ennemies.
 45 : Enlighten : A random proc 15% damage increase, that’s good to take
 46 – 48 : Mental strength 3/3 : 3% Casting speed and 10% intellect, take this talent, it’s very good.
 49 : Meditation 3/3 : Once again, quite filler here but i like this talent for the extra mana regen when fighting
 50 – 54 : Force of will 5/5 : This talent is NUTS, 5% Damage, 5% Crit and 20% upgrade on your shield. This is absolutely enormous, you want to take this.
 55 : Chastise : The boost component of this spell is not really useful, however this is a nice instant spell that gives you a bit more control, very cool.
 56 : Holy Nova : Finally your first and only AoE damaging spell. You could very much choose to take this WAY earlier (After Divine fury). You don’t always face AoE situations but this spell can be very strong once in a while.
 57 – 58 : Holy Focus 2/2 : You can now cast spells more easily when face tanking mobs
 59 – 60 : Improved shadow word : pain 2/2 : More damage on one of your damaging spell

The final spec would look like this :

![Image](https://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2025/38/4/1758225907-leveling.jpg)

This is only a version of what you can do, you’re free to experiment anything you want, that’s part of the fun. The final spec (31/13/7) is very reliable for solo content farming and i still use it after dinging 60.

The usual rotation of a discipline priest during leveling would be the following :
Holy Fire -> Smite -> Shadow Word Pain -> Wand till death of the monster

You can use Mind blast for the quick cast and extra burst but the mana cost is usually not worth it.

If you find yourself in some troubles, with a multiple pull for example, don't panic, the priest is a very strong solo class and has weapons to deal with this.
Fear your enemies and start focusing one to kill it as fast as possible, don't wand here, use your mana. When the mobs are in melee range don't hesitate to shield yourself. Heal yourself if you're getting low, rince and repeat.
With this strategy you can actually solo elites very easily as soon as you're getting some levels. Drop a lightwell, shield yourself before the pull and each time your shield CD is up. Use your mana to dps with spells and fear on CD to refresh shadow word pain and holy fire. Heal yourself with renew and the lightwell.

 ---
3. **Professions**

Turtle Wow made an incredible job making every profession interesting along the game. I cannot really advise you to go for a specific set of professions in order to min/max your character. It really depends on what you want to do. However here are some pointers that can help during and after the leveling :

Gathering professions (Skinning/Herbalism/Mining) are a GREAT way to make money reliably during the whole game. That's what i went for and it allowed me to make a confortable amount of money so i don't have to worry about buying my mount as lvl 40 or buying gear/enchants/consummables at lvl 60.
If you're aiming for this i would advise to sell absolutely everything you gather to vendors or the auction house and not to worry about keeping anything.

Crafting professions : While those won't help you make as much money in early game, it will help you quite a lot and might be very profitable when reaching high levels. As a priest, the most notable and useful for you would be :
 - Tailoring : You will be able to craft some gear during your leveling which is always enjoyable, if you reach 300/300 in tailoring you will also be able to craft <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14154> which is a great chest that you will keep for a long time.
 - Alchemy : In combination with Herbalism. You can make potions that will ease your journey, this will be quite profitable in late game with the correct recipes since every raid brings some potions.
 - Jewelcrafting : In combination with Mining. Nice but very expensive profession, you will be able to craft rings, trinkets and necks which are usually quite hard to find in early game. It is also profitable in end game due to some nice epic crafts and rare enchants.
 - Enchanting : Quite hard to level, but combined with Tailoring it will be a nice way to make a lot of money when you unlock late game enchants.

 ---
4. **What race should i pick ?**

Honestly, i think the best answer to this question is : just pick the race you like the most because you will end up playing a lot on this character so you don't want to be disgusted by it.
There is still some min/maxing to do depending on your race so i list here a few arguments :

Horde :
As a proud horde player you have two choices for your priest. The undead will feel smoother during the leveling because of its great racial spell Devouring Plague. It is also superior in PvP thanks to Will of the Forsaken that will clean Sleeps/Charms every once in a while. The undead also has a little bit more of intelligence which is nice for your mana pool (but really, not significant). Your other choice is troll. While the troll suffers from really terrible priest racial spells, it has the strongest PVE racial spell in the game in my opinion : Berserking. This spell will make you cast faster for 10seconds which can be a life saver in critical situations.

Alliance :
If you're crazy enough to pick alliance after seeing how sexy Trolls and Undeads are, you are a strange person. But i'm no one to judge. In my opinion the best choice for alliance players in PvE are Humans because of their increased mana regeneration rate and their racial that gives a strong instant self heal.

 ---
Let's now tackle the important part of this guide, which is raiding and playing your Holy priest.

As a healer your goal is to help your raid survive. While this role can give some pressure it is incredibly rewarding and in my opinion the funniest role in WoW.
The only thing you have to hope for is for your group to kill the boss so you don't face the old phrase every single non-healer player might say
> That's always the healer's fault

.

My advise to achieve this goal as much as possible is, first, to always have in mind a "priority" target list which would be :

 - You : If you're dead, who will heal the group ? Not the other heals because they were so bad they let you die. So if you're dying, save yourself first.
 - The tank : If the tank dies, the fight is most likely a wipe. Your job is to not allow the tank to die so focus him and always have an eye on his health bar.
 - The other heals : As we just said, the other heals are so bad they might let you die, however that's not a reason to seek vengeance. Save your healer friends since they will help you hold the rest of the raid alive.
 - DPS : If your raid doesn't have anymore damage, your mana bar will run low and the whole group will die. While it's less of a problem if one or two dps die and you can't do anything about it, don't let them all die or they will complain for ages !

 ---
5. **Healing priest statistics**

Here are the different important stats you want on your Priest :

 - Healing Power : Your primary stat, every single of your spell will scale on that, the more you have the better. And the more you have the stronger will be your down ranked spells which gives a better mana gestion.
 - Spell Crit : This stat is strong on healing priest since most of our spells (except shield and renew) can crit for 150% the amount of heal. In addition, a crit with any direct healing spell will buff our target for 25% more armor, which is huge on a tank.
 - Intellect : Intellect will give you a bigger mana bar and more spell crit. You want as much as possible
 - Spirit : Priests use spirit very well as they get Healing Power and mana regen from it. You want to have a lot of it. Since you're gonna have a lot of spirit you will have to care about the 5 seconds rule. Basically when you stop casting for 5 seconds your mana regenaration kicks in. For this reason it is interesting to try to heal completely your team then wait for several seconds to regen a bit of mana before healing again (if it's possible of course).
 - Mp5 : Helps you regen mana when you're casting, you'll find it on a lot of healing items, valuable stat.
 - Stamina : Gives you HP, more HP = you're less likely to die, which is good. But that's not a primary stat you have to hunt for.

 ---
6. **Healing priest spells**

To be a successful healer, a priest has a large arsenal of healing and utility spells that you have to use and i will give an overview here.
Something very important as a healer is to be very careful with his mana, since a healer that is Out Of Mana (OOM) is basically useless. To achieve this goal you have several tools (Potions, Mana regen) but one very important thing is down-ranking spells.
Down-ranking means using spells of a rank that is lower that the highest you learnt this results as a less powerful spell but also considerably less mana expensive !
I won’t go too much into details because i'm no master, and very experienced priests might use differents ranks than me.

Here are the healing spells i use in order to heal in raids :

 - Heal (Max rank) : This is your bread and butter heal, it is very mana efficient, scale a lot of your healing power and has a slow 2.5 second cast. If you are not in an emergency situation, use this spell.
 - Greater Heal (Max rank) : This is your strong and expensive heal. If your facing high sustained damages (for example each boss hit takes 50% of your tank life), use this spell. However be careful, this is very mana expensive and you will get OOM very fast if you spam this spell.
 - Flash heal (Max Rank) : This is your "Oh shit" heal. This is a fast casting, mana expensive spell that you want to use when you need to quickly heal several of your teammates, or if you see someone with critical health and you don't think you have 2.5s to cast another spell in order to save them
 - Renew (Max Rank) : Renew is a powerful and mana efficient Heal over Time (HoT). I usually like to have it 100% of the time on my tanks so it smoothes damage to make the healing easier.
 - Renew (Rank 5) : Renew scale very well on your healing power, so even if rank 5 renew is less strong than max rank, it remains a very good heal over time for almost no mana. You usually don't want to use this on your tanks but it's cool to cast it on other group members that took some damage if you don't want to bother casting another spell on them. It's also a nice way to heal people when you have to move.
 - Prayer of Healing (Max Rank) : This spell is extremely costly and long to cast and sadly you cannot cast it on someone that is not in your party. I would not recommand to use this spell without Inner focus. It is a great spell if your entire group just took a large chunk of damage and you want to heal everyone before saving the rest of the raid.
 - Prayer of healing (Rank 1) : Same idea but way less costly and powerful, if you don't have much to do and want to heal your entire party for a small chunk of damage, go for it.
 - Power word : Shield (Max rank) : This spell can sometimes be tricky to use, indeed, Warrior and Druid tanks might hate you for this because the damage tanked by the shield won't let them generate rage, so use it carefully. However this spell can be extremely powerful in different situations. It can help you mitigate incoming damage on a target if you're ready for it. It's also your BEST reaction when someone is on the verge of dying. If you see someone in your raid taking a lot of damage and reaching critical health, don't bother trying to hard cast a healing spell. Start with a shield to prevent him from dying and then you can heal safely. Having an instant spell to react to critical situations is one of the priests strengths.
 - Holy Nova (Max rank) : This one is not mandatory to take. It can be useful in some situations, giving a small burst of instant heal (with pre raid BIS gear you'll crit around 800). However this is mana expensive and very situational since it has a small range.
Then you have "utility spells"  :
 - Dispell Magic (Rank 2) : Strong instant spell that debuff 2 Magic effects, either negative on allies or positive on enemies. This spell can be extremely important depending on what you have to debuff, i recommand using the Add-On Decursive for easy use.
 - Abolish Disease : Instant spell, puts a buff on an ally that debuffs a disease effect every 5s for 20s, very useful and cheap. Use it when enemies cast annoying diseases.
 - Fade (Max Rank) : Instant spell, reduces your threat towards every enemy, very useful in fights when you pull aggro because of your healing. Please do not die stupidly when pulling agro from tanks by not using this spell.
 - Mana Burn (Max Rank) : Burns the mana of an enemy to deal some damages, very niche use but can be useful against bosses that you need to mana burn.
 - Psychic Screan (Max Rank) : Instant AoE fear, you usually DONT want to use this in raid.
 - Shackle Undead (Max Rank) : Nice control spell against undeads, can be useful to ease hard pulls or controls adds.
 - Inner Focus : 3 minute cooldown, your next spell doesn't cost mana and has +25% crit chance. Use it as a panic button to hope getting a big crit heal or when your mana is running very low (casting a 0 mana spell doesn't count during the 5s rule for mana regen). I prefer using it with greater heal or prayer of healing depending on the situation
And finally your buffs :
 - Power Word : Fortitude (Max Rank) : Stamina Buff, has to be up 100% of the time on the whole raid
 - Divine Spirit (Max Rank) : Your Spirit buff, has to be up 100% of the time on the whole raid (not really if they are melee but trolls do have some use for spirit so just do it).
 - Shadow Protection (Max Rank) : Shadow resistance buff, has to be up on the whole raid as long as the mobs have shadow spells/damage.
 - Proclaim Champion : This spell is the last talent from the Holy tree and is incredible. It makes your tank tankier, reducing its damages taken, increases its magic resistance and also gives you mana depending on the tank damages ! In addition it gives you cool spells that allows you to give your champion either 5% damage or +10% healing recieved as well as a battle res every hour. Take this spell and ALWAYS have it on your tank. If your raid has multiple priests or the tank doesn't need the tanking buff and you struggle with mana you can think of putting this on your highest DPS. But i think there is no case where this is actually beneficial to the raid.

 ---
7. **Talents**
Holy priests have different talent trees possible depending on your playstyle, your gear, what raid you're doing. However you can find 2 different types of build with some variants that i'm gonna explore a bit.

The first variant we will call the "Deep Holy Build". The goal here is to get at least 31 points in the Holy tree in order to get extremely strong healing talents as well as proclaim champion.

The base of this build would be (14/31/0) with several points free to place where you want, depending on your playstyle and your needs as you can see below :

![Image](https://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2025/38/5/1758236824-template-2.jpg)

With 6 free points that you can put in any talents highlighted in yellow. Some examples of builds (but not all of them) can be deeper in discipline (17/34/0):

![Image](https://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2025/38/5/1758236942-classic-holy.png)

Where you're getting the 15% shield buff in discipline for the extra chance to save someone in danger, as well as holy Nova for some instant AoE healing and Holy Reach for 6 increased yards on your holy spells which gives you a bit more flexibility in your positionning. However we can argue those last two talents are not very good and it's more interesting to grab raw heal output, with the deeper holy build (14/37/0) below for example :

![Image](https://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2025/38/5/1758236946-exemple-deep-holy.png)

But those builds are not the only ones, other talents, like spell warding can be strong in particular fights. It's your job to find the best one ! Usually i go for the (17/34/0) Build.

The second variant we will call the "Enlighten Build" (21/30/0). This build focuses on grabbing the enlighten talent deeper in the discipline tree by sacrificing Proclaim champion and some other holy talents. Enlighten is a strong spell than can buff your healing and a caster damage by 10% for 12s on a random proc when you cast a spell. It could be interesting to run this spec when you have too many deep holy priests in your raid or when your raid is overgeared and you wanna go for a speedrun. However in most situations i wouldn't recommand it. Here is an example :

![Image](https://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2025/38/5/1758237429-enlighten-spec.png)

 ---
8. **How to gear my priest**

Now that we're okay with the basics, it's time to get some gear, and especially what a lot of people will call "Pre Raid BIS Gear" which means the best gear you can obtain before accessing raids. Here is a list that you can follow that will give you a very good start for the early raids. If you obtain this gear, or pieces of equipement that are close, you are basically set to heal for MC, Onyxia, AQ 20, BWL, ZG, AQ 40.
Note that sometimes i don't show several pieces but one, it might be because there is no equivalent or just because i got lazy ! Also, when it comes to Holy priest, T1 raid set is pretty much garbage so don’t bother collecting it. Only several pieces will be better than the gear below.

Head :
 -	Best : Cowl of Mivax – Hivaxis, Karazhan Crypts <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83451>
 -	Great : Cassandra’s grace – BoE, World Drop <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13102>
 -	Great : Crimson Felt Hat – Magistrate Barthilas, Stratholme Undead <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18727>

Neck :
 -	Animated Chain Necklace – Ramstein The Gorger, Stratholme UD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18723>
 -	Hollowbone choker - Drifting avatar of sand, Black Morass <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61015>

Shoulders :
 -	Mantle of lost Hope – Lord Roccor – BRD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22234>

Cloak :
 -	Best : Hide of the wild – Tailoring <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18510>
This cloak is incredibly good and pretty cheap to get depending on your server, i recommand to get it as soon as possible.
 -	Good : Cloak of atonement – Damian, Stormwind Vault <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60500>

Chest :
 -	Best : Robes of the exalted – Baron Rivendare, Stratholme Undead <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13346>
 -	Great : Robe of the custodian - Wardens of Time reputation, Revered	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61002>

Bracers :
 -	Extremely well crafted cuffs – Epidamu, Black Morass	 <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=50431>

Hands :
 -	Hands of the exalted Herald – Princess Moira Bronzebeard, BRD	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12554>

Waist :
 -	Whipvine Cord – Alzzin The Wildshaper, Dire Maul East <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18327>

Legs :
 -	Padre’s trousers – Illyanna Ravenoak, Dire Maul West	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18386>

Boots :
 -	Boots of the holy mentor – Commander Andreon, Karazhan Crypts <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=50190>

Rings :
 -	Fordring’s Seal – In dreams Questline, Tyrion Fordring, Eastern Plaguelands	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=16058>
 -	Rosewine circle – Urok Doomhowl, LBRS <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13178>
 -	Deepearth signet – Corpsmuncher, Karazhan Crypts <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83460>

Trinkets :
 -	Royal Seal of Eldre’Thalas – Dire Maul quest trinket <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18469>
 -	Blessed Prayer Beads – Priest Sunken Temple Class quest <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19990>
These two trinkets are very easy to obtain and really good, get them.
 -	Second Wind – Golem Lord Argelmach, BRD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11819>
Less strong than the previous but has a nice +300 mana CD that can help sometimes.

Weapon 1H :
 -	The Hammer of Grace – Chest of the Seven, BRD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11923>
Try to get your hands on this hammer, you will run BRD a lot of times and if you get one of the two off hands it will be better than a 2H weapon.

Weapon 2H :
 -	Guiding Staff of Wisdom – Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, BRD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11932>

Off-Hand :
 -	Thaurissan’s Royal Scepter – Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, BRD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=11928>
 -	Tome of Divine Right – Mor Grayhoof, LBRS, T0.5 Questline	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22319>

Wand :
 -	Wand of Eternal Light – The Vault, BRD <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22254>
This might be annoying to get, if you don't just get any random wand with intellect, spirit or healing power on it.

 ---
9. **Enchants**

Now that you have some nice pieces of equipement, it is time to enchant it. Since this is a guide aimed for beginners, i’m not gonna cover the late game enchants (ZG, Naxx, Karazhan) since you should be aware of what you need when you reach this point ! Note that some enchants might be very expensive for the amount of stats they give. It’s your job to choose what to go for. I would say the minimum is Weapon, Hands and Bracers.

Leg / Head : Arcanum of focus (+12HP)	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18330>
Feet : Enchanted Armor Kit (+9HP)		<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61183>
Chest : Enchanted Armor Kit (+9HP) or +4 all stats
Hands : Healing Power (+30HP)
Weapon : Healing Power (+55HP)
Bracers : Healing Power (+23HP)
Rings / Neck : Beautiful Diamond Gemstone (+12HP)	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=56010>

 ---
10. **Consummables**

Finally the consummables ! Their usage will give your character a great performance boost that might be the difference between a successful pull and a wipe, but some might be expensive especially for new players. You will see with your guild what is absolutely necessary for raiding. The bare minimum are Mana Potions and Brilliant Mana Oil (cheap and very efficient).

Major Mana Potions : Mandatory, restores a lot of mana on a 2minute cooldown, if you have mana problems don't hesitate to use the first one early in the fight so you can use an extra one.	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13444>
Tea with Sugar <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=15723> / Nordanaar Hebal tea	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61675> : Emmergency heal/mana pot. Less important but might make a difference, try to farm some.
Dark / Demonic Runes <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=20520> / <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=12662> : Shares a CD with tea, sacrifice some health to get mana back.
Brilliant Mana Oil : Cheap and long duration buff that gives you healing power and Mp5, get it. <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=20748>
Empowering Herbal Salad : Healing power food.	<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83309>
Sagefish / Nightfin soup : Mp5 food, if you don't go for the salad go for this, it's pretty cheap.
Flask of distilled wisdom : +2000 mana for 2 hours. Might not be needed for easy raids and this is an expensive one. But if you have mana problems go for it. <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=13511>
Spirit of Zanza : +50 Stam/Spirit buff, very strong buff but you need to be revered with Zul'Gurub reputation to get it, try to farm the raid weekly for it. <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=20079>
Mageblood Potion : A nice a cheap mp5 boost in case you lack of mana <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=20007>

So here is the first version of the guide. I hope this will help people !
I will keep it updated so don't hesitate to share your thoughts in comments.
content_html:
Hello everyone, Picodon here, Holy priest. I wanted to share a quick priest guide i made, mostly for new players, hope it will be useful.
DISCLAIMER
I am not a professional priest neither am i a long time player on turtle wow. Hovewer i’ve been playing private wow servers for a while.
While searching on the forum, I didn’t find a beginner oriented guide for priests that would have helped me on my journey. I hope this one will help new priests players.
I do not say that i have the absolute truth backed by complex calculations, experienced players might find my guide not accurate enough and i would be more than happy to share about it in the comments as long as people remain normal and constructive human beings.
  1. Introduction

    This guide will focus on the Healing (i.e. Holy Priest). I advise to go this way after you hit 60 and intend to raid. Before this, i recommand to level as shadow or discipline (my favourite) spec since it will make solo farming WAY easier and still allow you to heal any dungeon in the game.

    The priest is a great tool in raiding environment for all the utility it brings. It is a very versatile healer who can apply Heal over Time, strong and slow direct heals, fast direct heals and some strong AoE healing (only for your group sadly) as well as an instant shield. While it’s not the best at anything the Holy priest is a great and reliable healer that fits any raid composition.
  2. Leveling

    As said, leveling as a priest is way easier as shadow or discipline. Leveling as holy is possible, however it will be slower and most likely less fun, i would not advise to go for it unless you are leveling in group.

    Here is a quick example of a Discipline leveling build. It allows good mana regeneration, better healing efficiency than shadow and a cool gameplay revolving around different spells and big crits giving you instant smites.

    10 – 11 : Wand Specialization : As a leveling priest you will wand, A LOT, this talent is the strongest you can pick.
    12 – 16 : Spirit tap 5/5 : It seems boring to take this early because it doesn’t give you more damage. However this talent alone will grant you a huge amount of mana regen and will make the difference between drinking every 3 pulls and almost not have to drink at all which is a CONSIDERABLE gain of time.
    17 – 21 : Divinity 5/5 : 5% crit on every holy spell is great since discipline heavily scale on crits
    22 – 26 : Divine fury 5/5 : -0.5 casting time on basically every single spell you will use, mandatory
    27 – 29 : Piercing light 3/3 : 6% Hit so you don’t miss your spells so often
    30 – 31 : Improved power word 2/2 : fortitude : Not mandatory, but i like this talent since PWF if a great buff that you will always have.
    32 – 34 : Mental agility 3/5 : Less mana used on offensive spells, renew, shield. That’s a nice talent that opens the new tiers.
    35 : Inner Focus : Every 3 min you have a free spell with more critical chance. Use it for a greater heal if you’re in a bad situation or for holy fire when you open on a monster.
    36 – 37 : Improved inner fire 2/2 : More spell power, you’re happy
    38 – 39 : Meditation 2/3 : Give you some mana regen while fighting. This is not mandatory but still good and opens the door to the real deal.
    40 – 41 : Purifying flames 2/2 : You ALWAYS open a fight with holy fire which means this talent is basically a 12% damage increase, what else ?
    42 – 44 : Searing light 3/3 : While this talent is not very reliable in early game since you don’t have a lot of critical chance. This talent gives the disco priest one of its biggest strength, instant big smites in the head of your ennemies.
    45 : Enlighten : A random proc 15% damage increase, that’s good to take
    46 – 48 : Mental strength 3/3 : 3% Casting speed and 10% intellect, take this talent, it’s very good.
    49 : Meditation 3/3 : Once again, quite filler here but i like this talent for the extra mana regen when fighting
    50 – 54 : Force of will 5/5 : This talent is NUTS, 5% Damage, 5% Crit and 20% upgrade on your shield. This is absolutely enormous, you want to take this.
    55 : Chastise : The boost component of this spell is not really useful, however this is a nice instant spell that gives you a bit more control, very cool.
    56 : Holy Nova : Finally your first and only AoE damaging spell. You could very much choose to take this WAY earlier (After Divine fury). You don’t always face AoE situations but this spell can be very strong once in a while.
    57 – 58 : Holy Focus 2/2 : You can now cast spells more easily when face tanking mobs
    59 – 60 : Improved shadow word : pain 2/2 : More damage on one of your damaging spell

    The final spec would look like this :



    This is only a version of what you can do, you’re free to experiment anything you want, that’s part of the fun. The final spec (31/13/7) is very reliable for solo content farming and i still use it after dinging 60.

    The usual rotation of a discipline priest during leveling would be the following :
    Holy Fire -> Smite -> Shadow Word Pain -> Wand till death of the monster

    You can use Mind blast for the quick cast and extra burst but the mana cost is usually not worth it.

    If you find yourself in some troubles, with a multiple pull for example, don't panic, the priest is a very strong solo class and has weapons to deal with this.
    Fear your enemies and start focusing one to kill it as fast as possible, don't wand here, use your mana. When the mobs are in melee range don't hesitate to shield yourself. Heal yourself if you're getting low, rince and repeat.
    With this strategy you can actually solo elites very easily as soon as you're getting some levels. Drop a lightwell, shield yourself before the pull and each time your shield CD is up. Use your mana to dps with spells and fear on CD to refresh shadow word pain and holy fire. Heal yourself with renew and the lightwell.

  3. Professions

    Turtle Wow made an incredible job making every profession interesting along the game. I cannot really advise you to go for a specific set of professions in order to min/max your character. It really depends on what you want to do. However here are some pointers that can help during and after the leveling :

    Gathering professions (Skinning/Herbalism/Mining) are a GREAT way to make money reliably during the whole game. That's what i went for and it allowed me to make a confortable amount of money so i don't have to worry about buying my mount as lvl 40 or buying gear/enchants/consummables at lvl 60.
    If you're aiming for this i would advise to sell absolutely everything you gather to vendors or the auction house and not to worry about keeping anything.

    Crafting professions : While those won't help you make as much money in early game, it will help you quite a lot and might be very profitable when reaching high levels. As a priest, the most notable and useful for you would be :
    • Tailoring : You will be able to craft some gear during your leveling which is always enjoyable, if you reach 300/300 in tailoring you will also be able to craft https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=14154 which is a great chest that you will keep for a long time.
    • Alchemy : In combination with Herbalism. You can make potions that will ease your journey, this will be quite profitable in late game with the correct recipes since every raid brings some potions.
    • Jewelcrafting : In combination with Mining. Nice but very expensive profession, you will be able to craft rings, trinkets and necks which are usually quite hard to find in early game. It is also profitable in end game due to some nice epic crafts and rare enchants.
    • Enchanting : Quite hard to level, but combined with Tailoring it will be a nice way to make a lot of money when you unlock late game enchants.
  4. What race should i pick ?

    Honestly, i think the best answer to this question is : just pick the race you like the most because you will end up playing a lot on this character so you don't want to be disgusted by it.
    There is still some min/maxing to do depending on your race so i list here a few arguments :

    Horde :
    As a proud horde player you have two choices for your priest. The undead will feel smoother during the leveling because of its great racial spell Devouring Plague. It is also superior in PvP thanks to Will of the Forsaken that will clean Sleeps/Charms every once in a while. The undead also has a little bit more of intelligence which is nice for your mana pool (but really, not significant). Your other choice is troll. While the troll suffers from really terrible priest racial spells, it has the strongest PVE racial spell in the game in my opinion : Berserking. This spell will make you cast faster for 10seconds which can be a life saver in critical situations.

    Alliance :
    If you're crazy enough to pick alliance after seeing how sexy Trolls and Undeads are, you are a strange person. But i'm no one to judge. In my opinion the best choice for alliance players in PvE are Humans because of their increased mana regeneration rate and their racial that gives a strong instant self heal.
    Let's now tackle the important part of this guide, which is raiding and playing your Holy priest.

    As a healer your goal is to help your raid survive. While this role can give some pressure it is incredibly rewarding and in my opinion the funniest role in WoW.
    The only thing you have to hope for is for your group to kill the boss so you don't face the old phrase every single non-healer player might say
    That's always the healer's fault
    .

    My advise to achieve this goal as much as possible is, first, to always have in mind a "priority" target list which would be :
    • You : If you're dead, who will heal the group ? Not the other heals because they were so bad they let you die. So if you're dying, save yourself first.
    • The tank : If the tank dies, the fight is most likely a wipe. Your job is to not allow the tank to die so focus him and always have an eye on his health bar.
    • The other heals : As we just said, the other heals are so bad they might let you die, however that's not a reason to seek vengeance. Save your healer friends since they will help you hold the rest of the raid alive.
    • DPS : If your raid doesn't have anymore damage, your mana bar will run low and the whole group will die. While it's less of a problem if one or two dps die and you can't do anything about it, don't let them all die or they will complain for ages !
  5. Healing priest statistics

    Here are the different important stats you want on your Priest :
    • Healing Power : Your primary stat, every single of your spell will scale on that, the more you have the better. And the more you have the stronger will be your down ranked spells which gives a better mana gestion.
    • Spell Crit : This stat is strong on healing priest since most of our spells (except shield and renew) can crit for 150% the amount of heal. In addition, a crit with any direct healing spell will buff our target for 25% more armor, which is huge on a tank.
    • Intellect : Intellect will give you a bigger mana bar and more spell crit. You want as much as possible
    • Spirit : Priests use spirit very well as they get Healing Power and mana regen from it. You want to have a lot of it. Since you're gonna have a lot of spirit you will have to care about the 5 seconds rule. Basically when you stop casting for 5 seconds your mana regenaration kicks in. For this reason it is interesting to try to heal completely your team then wait for several seconds to regen a bit of mana before healing again (if it's possible of course).
    • Mp5 : Helps you regen mana when you're casting, you'll find it on a lot of healing items, valuable stat.
    • Stamina : Gives you HP, more HP = you're less likely to die, which is good. But that's not a primary stat you have to hunt for.
  6. Healing priest spells

    To be a successful healer, a priest has a large arsenal of healing and utility spells that you have to use and i will give an overview here.
    Something very important as a healer is to be very careful with his mana, since a healer that is Out Of Mana (OOM) is basically useless. To achieve this goal you have several tools (Potions, Mana regen) but one very important thing is down-ranking spells.
    Down-ranking means using spells of a rank that is lower that the highest you learnt this results as a less powerful spell but also considerably less mana expensive !
    I won’t go too much into details because i'm no master, and very experienced priests might use differents ranks than me.

    Here are the healing spells i use in order to heal in raids :
    • Heal (Max rank) : This is your bread and butter heal, it is very mana efficient, scale a lot of your healing power and has a slow 2.5 second cast. If you are not in an emergency situation, use this spell.
    • Greater Heal (Max rank) : This is your strong and expensive heal. If your facing high sustained damages (for example each boss hit takes 50% of your tank life), use this spell. However be careful, this is very mana expensive and you will get OOM very fast if you spam this spell.
    • Flash heal (Max Rank) : This is your "Oh shit" heal. This is a fast casting, mana expensive spell that you want to use when you need to quickly heal several of your teammates, or if you see someone with critical health and you don't think you have 2.5s to cast another spell in order to save them
    • Renew (Max Rank) : Renew is a powerful and mana efficient Heal over Time (HoT). I usually like to have it 100% of the time on my tanks so it smoothes damage to make the healing easier.
    • Renew (Rank 5) : Renew scale very well on your healing power, so even if rank 5 renew is less strong than max rank, it remains a very good heal over time for almost no mana. You usually don't want to use this on your tanks but it's cool to cast it on other group members that took some damage if you don't want to bother casting another spell on them. It's also a nice way to heal people when you have to move.
    • Prayer of Healing (Max Rank) : This spell is extremely costly and long to cast and sadly you cannot cast it on someone that is not in your party. I would not recommand to use this spell without Inner focus. It is a great spell if your entire group just took a large chunk of damage and you want to heal everyone before saving the rest of the raid.
    • Prayer of healing (Rank 1) : Same idea but way less costly and powerful, if you don't have much to do and want to heal your entire party for a small chunk of damage, go for it.
    • Power word : Shield (Max rank) : This spell can sometimes be tricky to use, indeed, Warrior and Druid tanks might hate you for this because the damage tanked by the shield won't let them generate rage, so use it carefully. However this spell can be extremely powerful in different situations. It can help you mitigate incoming damage on a target if you're ready for it. It's also your BEST reaction when someone is on the verge of dying. If you see someone in your raid taking a lot of damage and reaching critical health, don't bother trying to hard cast a healing spell. Start with a shield to prevent him from dying and then you can heal safely. Having an instant spell to react to critical situations is one of the priests strengths.
    • Holy Nova (Max rank) : This one is not mandatory to take. It can be useful in some situations, giving a small burst of instant heal (with pre raid BIS gear you'll crit around 800). However this is mana expensive and very situational since it has a small range.
    Then you have "utility spells" :
    • Dispell Magic (Rank 2) : Strong instant spell that debuff 2 Magic effects, either negative on allies or positive on enemies. This spell can be extremely important depending on what you have to debuff, i recommand using the Add-On Decursive for easy use.
    • Abolish Disease : Instant spell, puts a buff on an ally that debuffs a disease effect every 5s for 20s, very useful and cheap. Use it when enemies cast annoying diseases.
    • Fade (Max Rank) : Instant spell, reduces your threat towards every enemy, very useful in fights when you pull aggro because of your healing. Please do not die stupidly when pulling agro from tanks by not using this spell.
    • Mana Burn (Max Rank) : Burns the mana of an enemy to deal some damages, very niche use but can be useful against bosses that you need to mana burn.
    • Psychic Screan (Max Rank) : Instant AoE fear, you usually DONT want to use this in raid.
    • Shackle Undead (Max Rank) : Nice control spell against undeads, can be useful to ease hard pulls or controls adds.
    • Inner Focus : 3 minute cooldown, your next spell doesn't cost mana and has +25% crit chance. Use it as a panic button to hope getting a big crit heal or when your mana is running very low (casting a 0 mana spell doesn't count during the 5s rule for mana regen). I prefer using it with greater heal or prayer of healing depending on the situation
    And finally your buffs :
    • Power Word : Fortitude (Max Rank) : Stamina Buff, has to be up 100% of the time on the whole raid
    • Divine Spirit (Max Rank) : Your Spirit buff, has to be up 100% of the time on the whole raid (not really if they are melee but trolls do have some use for spirit so just do it).
    • Shadow Protection (Max Rank) : Shadow resistance buff, has to be up on the whole raid as long as the mobs have shadow spells/damage.
    • Proclaim Champion : This spell is the last talent from the Holy tree and is incredible. It makes your tank tankier, reducing its damages taken, increases its magic resistance and also gives you mana depending on the tank damages ! In addition it gives you cool spells that allows you to give your champion either 5% damage or +10% healing recieved as well as a battle res every hour. Take this spell and ALWAYS have it on your tank. If your raid has multiple priests or the tank doesn't need the tanking buff and you struggle with mana you can think of putting this on your highest DPS. But i think there is no case where this is actually beneficial to the raid.
  7. Talents
    Holy priests have different talent trees possible depending on your playstyle, your gear, what raid you're doing. However you can find 2 different types of build with some variants that i'm gonna explore a bit.

    The first variant we will call the "Deep Holy Build". The goal here is to get at least 31 points in the Holy tree in order to get extremely strong healing talents as well as proclaim champion.

    The base of this build would be (14/31/0) with several points free to place where you want, depending on your playstyle and your needs as you can see below :



    With 6 free points that you can put in any talents highlighted in yellow. Some examples of builds (but not all of them) can be deeper in discipline (17/34/0):



    Where you're getting the 15% shield buff in discipline for the extra chance to save someone in danger, as well as holy Nova for some instant AoE healing and Holy Reach for 6 increased yards on your holy spells which gives you a bit more flexibility in your positionning. However we can argue those last two talents are not very good and it's more interesting to grab raw heal output, with the deeper holy build (14/37/0) below for example :



    But those builds are not the only ones, other talents, like spell warding can be strong in particular fights. It's your job to find the best one ! Usually i go for the (17/34/0) Build.

    The second variant we will call the "Enlighten Build" (21/30/0). This build focuses on grabbing the enlighten talent deeper in the discipline tree by sacrificing Proclaim champion and some other holy talents. Enlighten is a strong spell than can buff your healing and a caster damage by 10% for 12s on a random proc when you cast a spell. It could be interesting to run this spec when you have too many deep holy priests in your raid or when your raid is overgeared and you wanna go for a speedrun. However in most situations i wouldn't recommand it. Here is an example :

author: Menelluin
subject: Power word : shield and rage
content_md:
Hello, I would like to clarify something about the priest's shield on this server.
The other day, another priest player told me that several players on the server had given him a bit of grief because he was using his shield on a warrior tank and that it was hurting his aggro.
I've played on many private servers, and it turns out that on one of them, this was indeed the case, so I'm not surprised by this comment. However, I've been playing this class for a long time and I still play it on the official server, where this is NOT the case, as the log shows. The priest's shield does not normally prevent warriors or druids transformed into bears from generating rage. So my question is simple: “When people claim this here, is it an urban legend based on false memories, or is it actually a specific property of this server?”

author: Azcron
subject: Re: Power word : shield and rage
content_md: This actually comes down to which client you’re playing on. Back in 1.12 Vanilla, warriors and bears only generated rage when they actually took damage, so if you put Power Word: Shield on them it would absorb the hit completely and deny them rage, which is why people complained that shielding tanks hurt their threat. That mechanic stayed in place until patch 2.0.1 (the pre–Burning Crusade patch), when Blizzard changed it so that rage was calculated based on damage before absorption, meaning tanks still got their rage even if the shield ate the hit. From that point onward, including retail today and most private servers that use updated clients, shielding no longer interferes with rage generation. So if you’re on a true 1.12 emulation server, like Turtle, the complaints are real and not an urban legend, but if you’re on retail or a server running newer mechanics, shielding is perfectly safe and doesn’t block rage at all.

author: Menelluin
subject: Holy Nova
content_md:
I had a quick question about the Holy Nova. As much as I appreciate the developers' idea of ​​creating mechanics to slightly lower the Nova's mana cost, I don't understand another point. The Holy Nova is already a fairly specific skill that can't be used in all circumstances, even on these servers, so why remove what, in my opinion, was its main strength on a standard server? Namely, the fact that it generates absolutely no threat in healing or dps? Was this change motivated by other particularities of the Turtle WoW servers? This spell is weaker and more expensive than its counterpart for the mage. On groups of small enemies it had only one advantage: being able to be spammed immediately with the only constraint being mana. This stabilized the tank's life and melee while momentarily producing very decent damage. Now, I find it almost unusable in instances because even with a "low threat level," I often find myself reverting to tanks' secondary targets as soon as I use the spell as originally intended.
So my question is: "Is there something at high level that I don't yet perceive that motivates this choice? Is there a hidden power that I don't yet perceive in this spell on this server that counteracts this nerf?"
Thanks in advance to anyone who takes the time to shed some light on this. =)

author: Sharmaine
subject: Add scaling to priest talents
content_md:
Right now holy talent Improved Renew as well as Discipline talents Improved Power Word: Shield and Force of Will do not benefit from priest stats, making them lackluster in late game.

Improved Renew is widely known as a trap talent: this is because main draw of renew is in its 85% healing power scaling starting from rank 3. With 1000 healing power, rank 3 renew heals for 1025 over 15 sec for almost no mana, making it great choice for long fights. However, talent Improved renew doesn't serve priests that use renew for efficient healing at all! Because it only affects base healing. For renew it's 175 at rank 3, and 825 at rank 10. 15% of that is 26 (5 per tick when my ticks with 1000 healing power heal for 200+) and 123 (24 per tick when it ticks for over 350). Max rank renew is mana inefficient, and talent only boosts it for 7% at 1000 healing power. For downranked spells which all skilled priests use it might as well not exist at all. Yet it costs 3 point to level. I hope this explains why most priests that are aware of it not having scaling consider it a trap option.

Improved Power Word: Shield and Force of Will suffer of the same problem. However, most people aren't aware of this, since shield talents are in disc tree that is used for dps now, and game doesn't show numbers correctly on the ui, it requires some deliberate testing to know the truth.
Here's the formula for rank 10 Power word: Shield:
 942 * (1 + 0.15 IPWS + 0.2 FW) + healing_power*0.35
In short, talents don't affect bonus gained from healing power scaling.
Improved power world shield adds 142 for 3 talent points.
Force of Will adds 188 for 5 talent points.
Pretty good for pvp disc priests with no healing power to talk about, I guess, but becomes obsolete for healers once they've picked up some good gear in my opinion.

Okay, done with explanations, now towards suggestion.

I suggest that either scaling is added to these talents, or the effect is reworked. Static bonuses with no scaling do not belong in classic+ talent design! Priest is one of the few classes that is stuck being vanilla when everyone else got improvements!
One rework suggestion for renew is to make it tick faster. Right now druid HoTs tick every 2 seconds. Renew is every 3 seconds. It makes it hard to compete in effective healing with druids on meters since their dots just heal more often and top the targets off.
As for Improved Shield talent, at least fix the description so that you don't deceive holy priest healers! 17/34/0 is the most popular healer priest build that takes this talent, if people knew it only adds measly 142 hp to rank 10 shield no matter if they have 1.5k healing power they'd stop speccing into it! But of course I'd love shielding to be viable strategy too... People miss the disc healer.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Re: Add scaling to priest talents
content_md:
I wasn't even aware these talents work like that. I always believed in what description says, thanks.

Now some math. Let's suppose Priest has 1000 healing power and both IPWS and FW talents. So with the formula:
 942 * (1 + 0.15 IPWS + 0.2 FW) + healing_power*0.35
shield absorbs 1621.7 HP.

If we made scaling real, the formula would look like:
(942 + healing_power*0.35) * (1 + 0.15 IPWS + 0.2 FW)
and shield would absorb 1744.2 HP.

That's 122.5 HP difference. Is it much?

subject: Love the Disci - Hows my fellow Clerics?
content_md:
Hey, i didnt find a better forum for this but probably fits good here.

I wanted to Tell the Team how much i love the smite priest abilities, never was a big priest Player but the Chastising-Bishop-Cleric fantasy with the less xpensive instant smites and Support Buffet is incredibly rewarding.

Love to help out a heal/tank with shields or the whole group with healing prayer or enlightening/chastising my fellow DDs to buff. Really all in all a lot better than what official disci priest became.

So those who came up with this vibe of the class, great work.

Do my fellow clerics feel the same way? I read shadow wishes for some buffs and holy seems to still be great allround heal.

Also if some of you have item Suggestions for after MC please tell me! Am on Ambershire and while i dont minmax really i would love to have some goals outlined.

Have a nice day!

author: Tscosomaz
subject: My Two Cents about Disco Priest (and more)
content_md:
Hi gamers and devs, let's start saying you guys did a MAGNIFICENT job with class changes! For someone like me who still plays this version of the game since 20+ years, after one-year-long break from TWOW (missed 1.17.2, back with 1.18), what more than a brand new original spec, always considered a meme?

At Ambershire launch, motivated by theorycrafting goat, i said to myself "let's start with this new adventure, let's try Disco Priest and aim to the Seeker title!".

You guys, both devs and community, did a MAJESTIC job, having personally tested my three 60s on Nordanaar (Rogue, Pala and Mage), tested Disco Priest on Ambershire since launch, after two months of gameplay and first raids on a fresh server, i can say imo in pve all classes are, after all, quite balanced.

Very Very GZ, guys! In the past 20+ Years, "others" never were even close to what you have done!

As the title of the thread says, i'd like to express my personal thoughts about Discipline Priest, after having leveled as Disco, run 5men as Disco dps/heal and now running first raids as Disco dps.

Leveling was SOLID, being able to solo lot of quests many other classes could not.

In 5men, as dps, numbers are close to top magic-dps, spec has its own identity, rotation is not too complicate, but not too dumb.

I am playing Disco Priest as a support dps, buffing allies with Enlighten, Chastise and Grace of the Sunwell racial on cd, dispelling nasty debuffs and supporting with PW:S or Inner Focus big heals in critical situations.

As I always say: "if I wanted pure caster dps output, i would have rolled a Mage or a Lock, not a support-dps hybrid".

The spec has even an AOE-cleave option with Hoy Nova, but with actual mana pool, even with High Elf racial up, it's nearly a manatrap in cost/damage ratio (due to the "splitting" of the sp contribution between damage and heal components), more useful in solo-farming than spell-cleave, but maybe with better or dedicated gear the situation would improve, cant say. Anyway, Priest was not supposed to be an AOE-cleaver and just the option to support on spell-cleaving is something to thank for.

In low tier raids, for now, damage numbers still stay not too far from top magic h-dps classes...

On the other hand, with higher tier raids, if the support this spec would add to the raid is less than the pure numbers given by an h-dps dedicated class (read this like: why i should get in a Raid a Disco dps Priest if another Mage/Lock give to the raid more benefits?), in my vision, if this occurs, it would mean the existence of some kind of "unbalance".

Sadly, i truly fear that for Disco dps the awful item-scaling from sets, with the lack o any useful item in t1-t2 bracket, will led to "unbalance", unless niche fights. For sure, Priests from Nordanaar can be more accurate about.

Talents:
IMHO, the only Discipline talent that should need a little rework is Resurgent Shield <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=45560>

 *When your Power Word: Shield is broken, 25% of its base mana cost is refunded and increases damage and healing done by Holy spells and effects by up to 10% of the shield's total absorption amount for 8 sec.*

With actual settings:
 - it is a "pvp talent", for a spec that in pvp would be "just-ok" if properly mastered;
+ in pve, it might be useful in some niche ranged tanking fights, but nothing more;
 - in pve, the buff nearly never procs in leveling, very rarely procs in 5men and always with awful timing (due to its design). In some raid fights with aoe damage suffered, the procs might be a biiiit more good-timed (just to stay optimistic and polite :P).

I've read someone saying on other posts that this is a talent designed for pvp (and this is true), but why not reworking a bit this great idea that replaced Reflective Shield, keeping all its features and just adding a more controlled usage and (above all) a support effect on allies, in line with the identity of the spec?

My suggestion:

 *When you cast Power Word: Shield on yourself, increases damage and healing done by your Holy spells and effects by up to 10% of the shield's total absorption amount for 8 sec. When your Power Word: Shield expires or is broken, the shielded target is energized with 3% total mana, 20 rage or 30 energy.*

+ the personal buff stays the same, what would change is WHEN you gain it;
+ added an average support effect with great versatility, giving something "back" also when the Shield is not broken by damage (atm a total mana waste);
+ pvp impact of the talent would not be affected, in addition it would be more versatile and useful also in leveling, dungeon and raid;
+ PW:S would become a third buff to watch, like Inner Fire and Purifying Flames, adding more "spice" to pve rotation;
+ due to Weakened Soul debuff, the energizing boost would occour just once every 15secs per target, making it all but overpowered.
+ adding the "When your PW:S expires" part is mandatory imo. The point is: what is the reason to spend 4 talent picks for something that has a chance to not even occour?

Improved Renew, Improved Power Word: Shield, Force of Will
Checking other posts on the forum, many people dont like these talents only affecting base amounts. IMHO they would be too overpowered otherwise:

 - Improved Renew is a Row1 talent, designed for leveling, when your gear gives nearly no +heal. In raiding, huge contribution from +heal is what makes Renew mana-efficient. Letting Improved Renew scaling with gear would make it too powerful in endgame. There is another way to make this talent attractive...
 - PW:S would be a too overpowered istant cast if talents would scale with equip, unbalancing expecially pvp.
 - Improved Renew is considered a "trap" by many, but "forcing" the picks, improving a bit Swift Recovery (read below) might change the consideration about it and maybe make more build options available.

A "New" Vanilla Archetype: Disco Healer?
A lot of ppl miss Disco Priest... I think with couple marginal changes to some talents, a new Raid archetype would raise, very close to the wotlk Disco: an healer focused mainly on Raid, using PW:S, Renew and Flash Heal. I think about some raid fights with massive aoe damage and how they could be a lot easier with even only one Disco shielding raiders. Later in this post, during my thougts about itemization, the hybrid nature of the spec will show how this archetype can play as healer or as dps even in the same fight (more dps-oriented or more heal-oriented, depending on talents setup).

What would let this archetype work?
+ mainly, the scaling to PW:S from gear in TWOW: the contribution is huge, even with talents only affecting base amount, considering that originally it was 0.

What does not let atm this archetype work fine?
 - The 4 secs cd on PW:S. This would be solved reducing the PW:S cd to 3secs via Improved Power Word: Shield third pick (<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=14769>). Why to 3 secs? This is the mandatory line: you can cast a PW:S, followed by a Renew or Flash Heal, then a new PW:S on another target. With a 4secs cd you have 2 gcds before you can cast another PW:S. Reworking the bonus-set from some Priest sets (they all are terrible for Disco), the cd could be even lowered or maybe removed (i would not like that last option, tho, imo a PW:S spam is not suited for vanilla).
 - No "benefit" from the Weakened Soul debuff. Weakened Soul is what prevents the PW:S spam on the same target; imo its ok as it is, no need to lower the duration, 15secs is enough, even more duration could be a benefit IF the debuff would give some other side-effect via items or talents. In example, i would recommend to add to Swift Recovery (<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=51485>) in Holy tree something like "and by 5/10% if the target is affected by Weakened Soul". This little change by itself would create couple new talent build options, "forcing" the pick of Improved Renew and making it attractive.
 - Absence of Penance and Circle of Healing. No need imo, vanilla is not suited for Penance and Circle of Healing: Penance would unbalance pvp and Circle of Healing would unbalance raids. Moreover, i like a lot Chastise as it is, not a game-changing capstone, even if I would have added a direct support effect (mana/rage/energy gain on target) in place of the huge haste buff. Again, reworking the Priest bonus sets is the way to give solidity to this archetype and whole class.
 - Shielded Warrior/Bears not gaining rage. As i said at the start of this post, i missed last year of twow... Couple game friends are sure that after 1.17.2 devs changed the vanilla mechanic and atm shielded ragers can keep to gain rage. I have checked all the changelogs on forum and no info confirmed any change to the original mechanic. For me and for many on forum it works like it originally worked in 1.12 (no rage gain for shielded targets). Anyway, not an issue, expecially if you add a rage gain when PW:S expires or breaks on targets (via Resurgent Shield), as I suggested above; just dont shield ragers on pull unless they ask for it and keep PW:S on ragers only as a panic support button.

Itemization
This is the sore point. Liking versatility above all, I really hate dedicated +source items (+heal above all), but I understand this is an ancient setup too hard to let it go away. In the last years, however, a lot of hybrid +sp+heal items have been added or reworked, like priest t0.5/1/2, meaning there is an open-minded approach about the topic. This is the right approach imo, but it appears to have been stopped half-way, making sometimes the distribution of numbers and affects on many items totally "weird". This is due just to an "uncorrect" prospective in itemization affects-weightning during new items creation/reworking.

Let's make an example:
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22267> considered the pre-raid bis (couple super expensive options from Jewelcrafting). What next as Disco?
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22080> t0.5 (without considering the "struggle" to complete the quest chain): less sp, +crit (weight7) in place of +spellhit (weight19 if undercap, spec needs 10% from items. This big "unbalance" between spellcrit and spellhit, compared to other classes, is due to the lack of any source of +critdamage in talents. This leads to a loss of impact of Searing Light, the core mechanic of the spec itself).
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=16813> t1: the whole set is just +heal addition to T0.5, but lacks of 3% spellhit of T0,5 and any Shadow set, invalidating the whole set for Disco. In general, more int (just mana, crit/int conversion for Priest is an awful 1:64) and more Spirit (the +sp from talents is amazing, but too low ratio if compared with other classes pure +sp...) dont anything if there is no +sp increase... Moreover, SPI to mp5 Priest great conversion rate cannot be direcly translated into damage output). For Disco, +heal only affects healing side of the spec, unless the nearly null contribution via Resurgent Shield actual design.
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=16921> t2: like t1, a mere addition of some stats and a biiiit more +sp+heal, still no +spellhit, invalidating also this tier for Disco.
If you check TWOW db, the first item to improve Drakki helm is Mish'undare from Nefarian (last tier2 fight)...
In higher tiers, there is the unbalanced t2.5 set (for that one, a whole separated consideration must be done), only offset items in endgame content.

What showed for the Head slot happens also for mainly all the other slots: after T0,5 there is nothing, unless offsets or T2.5.

Mages and Locks can rely on their t1 and t2 sets, Disco Priest cant.

How Disco designed items might be?
+ as i said before, hybrid +sp+heal is the right approach for Disco, not +Holy.
+ Priest items must have Spirit stat, it is class core identity (unless Shadow).
+ just adding +heal to +sp affects, as done for T1 and T2, always led to a loss of power compared to other dedicated classes; the latter could be ok if "partially" compensated by the Spirit contribution to +sp and mp5 (less damage, more mana in longer fights), but we know that raid fights long enough to make this benefit something real and not only something on paper maybe 2-3.

Checking TWOW db, for some item slots, there are offsets not specificly designed for Disco that can be recycled, but many of them are not available yet on a fresh server, making the archetype struggling proper item scaling in almost every slot.

Above all, ignoring a-priori all the class sets for bad design is simply sad :(

My suggestion about Priest tiers:
+ a rework of Priest Tier1 and Tier2 sets, not creating a third +Holy set, the hybrid approach is the right one...
 - some bonus-set should be removed or reworked;
 - the core issue: Priest Tier1 and Tier2 do not give a single %spellhit bonus: t0.5 gives +3%, any Shadow set gives +3%, so any Disco Priest set MUST give at least 3%... The spec needs 10% from gear, Shadow only needs 6%.
+ take what follows into consideration: +spellhit has no effect on healing and +heal has no effect on dps. Given the hybrid nature of the spec, reworked items with both
+spellhit and +heal would not be overweighted in any way, just versatile.

The solution is so simple: just add +3% spellhit to t1 and t2, in item slots where there is no +crit already. And rework set bonuses...

Set bonuses thoughts
T0.5: Priest, Mage and Lock have a senseless 4set bonus pvp-oriented. After 20+ years, i still really struggle to understand the reason of a pvp-oriented bonus in a dungeon set. I strongly suggest to rework 4item-set bonus for all three previous classes, changing to something like the Paladin/Shaman chance on cast +sp proc or Druid chance on cast mana regain proc. You guys have done another AMAZING job reworking t0,5, anyway!
T1: only 5item-set bonus has a minimal impact on Disco and it's originally intended for heals.
T2: no impact on Disco.
ZG: +heal set. Imo it needs to be converted to hybrid +sp+heal. Bonus set are both acceptable and could be recycled on hybrid sets.
Aq20: +heal set. Imo it needs to be completely reworked, converted to hybrid +sp+heal (just to stay in line with the tier attitude). Bonus sets are senseless (one for Shadow and one pvp-oriented). Need to be completely changed.
Aq40: +Holy dps dedicated set. Not a fan. Lets be honest, this set is unbalanced and appears to be a compensation given in an already progressed server to long time players... 2item-set bonus is fine, 5item-set bonus is maybe the most senseless proc i have ever seen, really curious to question who originally had the idea, just to know what was in mind XD A better 5item-set bonus would be something like "Smite has a chance to increase the remaining duration of Chastise Haste buff on yourself" or "Smite has a chance to refresh the duration of Chastise Haste buff on yourself to its original duration". I suggest to rework to hybrid +heal+sp, +Holy is not the right approach for this archetype, lets +Holy items to stay on offset items…
T3: +heal set. It's ok, considering the previous set was +Holy dedicated. Lot of offset items in this tier help in counterbalancing the absence of an hybrid set, but having one also in this tier would not be bad.
Kara40: considering this is the endgame, I would create 3 different sets for this tier and further (+sp+heal, +heal, +shadow) and not couple +sp items in +Shadow set...

Finally, i can suggest couple bonus set ideas for Disco:
 - reduced threat from Holy and Discipline offensive spells.
 - chance (moderate) on PW:S cast to reduce damage taken by the target.
 - increased chance to crit with priest heals on target affected by PW:S or Weakened Soul.
 - increased PW:S absorb amount at the cost of increased Weakened Soul duration.
 - chance (low) on PW:S cast to make your next Flash Heal an istant cast.
 - increase the duration of Purifying Flame buff and Holy Fire dot.
 - reduce the mana cost of Holy and Discipline offensive spells when Inner Fire is active.
 - increase the critical stike multiplier of Smite when Inner Fire is active.
 - Inner Fire charges and duration increased.

+ just adding +heal to +sp affects, as done for T1 and T2, always led to a loss of power compared to other dedicated classes; the latter could be ok if "partially" compensated by the Spirit contribution to +sp and mp5 (less damage, more mana in longer fights), but we know that raid fights long enough to make this benefit something real and not only something on paper maybe 2-3.

Checking TWOW db, for some item slots, there are offsets not specificly designed for Disco that can be recycled, but many of them are not available yet on a fresh server, making the archetype struggling proper item scaling in almost every slot.

Above all, ignoring a-priori all the class sets for bad design is simply sad :(

My suggestion about Priest tiers:
+ a rework of Priest Tier1 and Tier2 sets, not creating a third +Holy set, the hybrid approach is the right one...
- some bonus-set should be removed or reworked;
- the core issue: Priest Tier1 and Tier2 do not give a single %spellhit bonus: t0.5 gives +3%, any Shadow set gives +3%, so any Disco Priest set MUST give at least 3%... The spec needs 10% from gear, Shadow only needs 6%.
+ take what follows into consideration: +spellhit has no effect on healing and +heal has no effect on dps. Given the hybrid nature of the spec, reworked items with both
+spellhit and +heal would not be overweighted in any way, just versatile.

The solution is so simple: just add +3% spellhit to t1 and t2, in item slots where there is no +crit already. And rework set bonuses...

Set bonuses thoughts
T0.5: Priest, Mage and Lock have a senseless 4set bonus pvp-oriented. After 20+ years, i still really struggle to understand the reason of a pvp-oriented bonus in a dungeon set. I strongly suggest to rework 4item-set bonus for all three previous classes, changing to something like the Paladin/Shaman chance on cast +sp proc or Druid chance on cast mana regain proc. You guys have done another AMAZING job reworking t0,5, anyway!
T1: only 5item-set bonus has a minimal impact on Disco and it's originally intended for heals.
T2: no impact on Disco.
ZG: +heal set. Imo it needs to be converted to hybrid +sp+heal. Bonus set are both acceptable and could be recycled on hybrid sets.
Aq20: +heal set. Imo it needs to be completely reworked, converted to hybrid +sp+heal (just to stay in line with the tier attitude). Bonus sets are senseless (one for Shadow and one pvp-oriented). Need to be completely changed.
Aq40: +Holy dps dedicated set. Not a fan. Lets be honest, this set is unbalanced and appears to be a compensation given in an already progressed server to long time players... 2item-set bonus is fine, 5item-set bonus is maybe the most senseless proc i have ever seen, really curious to question who originally had the idea, just to know what was in mind XD A better 5item-set bonus would be something like "Smite has a chance to increase the remaining duration of Chastise Haste buff on yourself" or "Smite has a chance to refresh the duration of Chastise Haste buff on yourself to its original duration". I suggest to rework to hybrid +heal+sp, +Holy is not the right approach for this archetype, lets +Holy items to stay on offset items…
T3: +heal set. It's ok, considering the previous set was +Holy dedicated. Lot of offset items in this tier help in counterbalancing the absence of an hybrid set, but having one also in this tier would not be bad.
Kara40: considering this is the endgame, I would create 3 different sets for this tier and further (+sp+heal, +heal, +shadow) and not couple +sp items in +Shadow set...

Finally, i can suggest couple bonus set ideas for Disco:
- reduced threat from Holy and Discipline offensive spells.
- chance (moderate) on PW:S cast to reduce damage taken by the target.
- increased chance to crit with priest heals on target affected by PW:S or Weakened Soul.
- increased PW:S absorb amount at the cost of increased Weakened Soul duration.
- chance (low) on PW:S cast to make your next Flash Heal an istant cast.
- increase the duration of Purifying Flame buff and Holy Fire dot.
- reduce the mana cost of Holy and Discipline offensive spells when Inner Fire is active.
- increase the critical stike multiplier of Smite when Inner Fire is active.
- Inner Fire charges and duration increased.

author: Alaythan
subject: Re: Shadow Priest issues
content_md:
Here are some proposed changes/updates to shadow priest to make it more competitive and enticing as a spec.

Talent changes:
Revert: Blackout to 3 second stun duration OR change it so each tick of shadow damage from the caster has a chance to stun for 2 seconds with an internal CD.
Move: Shadowform moved to level 30 talent.
Add: Hex (lvl 40 talent) (traditionally, always a shadow spell since the dawn of classic wow). Cast by Vile Priestess Hexx, Smolderthorn Shadow Priest, Sandfury Shadowhunter, Atal'ai Witchdoctor (the only one not slightly related to shadow priest).
Move Vampiric Embrace to level 20 talent row.
Vampiric Touch remains on lvl 30 talent row, requiring Vampiric Embrace.
Mind Flay: Now a baseline spell learned at level 20 (or sooner, maybe even 18 since it sucks worse than wanding without spell damage gear)

Baseline Change:
Shadow Word: Pain - now does 1 tick of damage on initial cast. Duration decreased by 3 seconds to compensate for 1 free tick. Now scales with haste (decreasing time between ticks of damage, and simultaneously decreasing duration to compensate for decreased tick windows)

Mind Flay: now scales with haste, similar to Arcane mages.

Add Shadow Word: Death - only usable while target is below 35% health. Does execute worthy damage, with a cooldown of 12 seconds. Costs % of maximum mana (not base mana), deals damage to caster = 20% of damage.

These are some random ideas I've had. I hope many people, especially shadow priest enthusiasts agree with me on the Hex talent change.
